explanation: In C++, the token pasting operator (##) is used within macro definitions to concatenate two tokens into a single token during macro expansion. This feature allows for dynamic generation of variable names, function names, or other identifiers, enabling more flexible and generic macro-based code. It is particularly useful in metaprogramming scenarios where code needs to adapt based on macro parameters, facilitating code reuse and reducing boilerplate in template-heavy or macro-driven codebases.
